subject: Termination proration & refund matrix for multi-year prepay
messages:
From: Lisa Carter <lisa.carter@nimbushealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Nimbus Health Finance <finance@nimbushealth.com>
Date: Fri, 8 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Termination clause & refund calc for our 3yr prepay

Kim —

Thanks for the call earlier. We reviewed Redwood's standard prepay terms and have a few redlines from finance/legal that touch termination and refund mechanics. High level: our procurement team is trying to keep options to exit within 90 days for structural changes, but they're willing to accept a financial reconciliation.

Specific asks:
- We want a clear refund matrix showing how much of an unused prepay is refundable on early termination (including examples for ramped consumption).
- If Redwood retains an \"unamortized\" portion, we need the calculation method (daily vs monthly) and a cap on holdback.
- Co-terming: We may want to align Redwood to our other vendor renewals in month 18; what credit language would you propose?

Attached is our proposed redline that currently replaces the refund section with a flat-90-day no-fault termination with no refund — that will not work for us. Can you propose middle-ground language we can show procurement? Also, do you have an example calculation for a $3,000,000 three-year prepay with a 12/24/36 month ramp (30%/35%/35%) where they exit after 18 months?

Would appreciate a quick call if you prefer.

Thanks,
Lisa Carter
CFO, Nimbus Health
Attachment: nimbus_proposed_redline.docx
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.inference.com>
To: Lisa Carter <lisa.carter@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.inference.com, monica_patel@redwood.inference.com
Date: Fri, 8 Jul 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Termination clause & refund calc for our 3yr prepay

Lisa —

Thanks for the clear note and the redline. Looping in Markus (legal) and Monica (account lead) so we can align on contract language and provide the calculator you asked for.

High-level position from sales: we can make a pragmatic compromise that preserves your flexibility while protecting Redwood for committed capacity and ramp-related provisioning. Two practical options for procurement to consider:

Option A — Amortized refund with proportional ramp adjustment
- Prepay is amortized monthly over the committed term. On early termination, unused amortized balance is refundable, minus an administrative reconciliation equal to three months of average committed spend (to cover provisioning and reserved capacity).
- Ramp adjustment: when usage has not reached full committed percentage, we normalize to an \"effective consumption\" curve (example calc below).

Option B — Escrow holdback + step-down exit credit
- A modest holdback (5-10%) retained in escrow for the first 12 months, released pro rata thereafter. Early exit triggers a refund of the remaining balance less a step-down fee that declines over time (e.g., 20% year1, 10% year2, 0% year3).

For co-terming: we typically provide a co-term credit equal to the remaining amortized prepay balance multiplied by the ratio of remaining months to the new co-term window — or, alternatively, a one-time credit applied to the next invoice to align renewal dates. Markus, see below for legal-preferred wording.

I'll attach a simple calculator that walks through the $3M example and a redline candidate for clause language. Would you be available 1:30–2:30pm PT today for a quick walk-through?

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.inference.com
Attachment: refund_prorate_calculator.xlsx
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.inference.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.inference.com>, Lisa Carter <lisa.carter@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Fri, 8 Jul 2027 12:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Termination clause & refund calc for our 3yr prepay

Lisa / Kim / Monica —

Thanks — I reviewed Nimbus' proposed redline and prepared a draft replacement section that balances early-exit flexibility with a predictable refund methodology. Key points from the redline (high-level):

1) Refund calculation: unused prepay balance will be calculated on a daily basis using amortization across the committed term. Daily amortization reduces disputes in ramp scenarios.

2) Administrative reconciliation: Redwood may deduct an administrative reconciliation fee equal to the lesser of (i) three months of the average monthly committed value or (ii) 10% of the unused prepay balance. This creates a predictable cap for Nimbus.

3) Ramp normalization: consumption for refund purposes will be normalized to the committed schedule. If actual usage is below the committed ramp percentage at the time of termination, Redwood will treat the shortfall as consumed for calculation of refund (i.e., no double-credit). Example calculations included in the attached redline and calculator.

4) Co-term credit: if customer elects to co-term with a third-party vendor within the committed term, customer may elect to apply remaining amortized balance as a pro-rated credit toward the next invoice. The credit calculation will be the remaining unused amortized balance multiplied by (remaining months / original remaining months) with a one-time processing fee of $5,000 for administrative alignment (waivable for enterprise deals).

5) Notice: 30 days' written notice for termination; refunds processed within 60 days of effective termination date.

I've attached the draft legal text (nimbus_redline_termination_v2.docx). If that structure is acceptable to Nimbus, the next step is to populate the example calculation.

Markus Klein
General Counsel, Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.inference.com
Attachment: nimbus_redline_termination_v2.docx

Kim / Markus / Monica —

Thanks, that all looks reasonable. The daily amortization with a capped administrative reconciliation gives us the predictability we need. Two quick follow-ups before we take this back to procurement:

1) Can you share the $3M example populated using Option A (daily amortization + 3-month admin cap) showing the refund amount if Nimbus exits on day 548 (roughly month 18)? Please show the ramp normalization math.

2) Can you confirm whether the processing fee for co-terming is competitive — $5,000 is OK but procurement may ask to waive for our enterprise package.

We can do a 20-minute screen share tomorrow morning if that helps.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Lisa
Lisa Carter
CFO, Nimbus Health
